questions.text: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Sun, araw.

questions.text: What is Earth's only natural satellite?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Moon, buwan, Luna.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the "Red Planet"?
What is the largest planet in our solar system?
Which planet is most famous for its bright, wide rings?
questions.hostNotes: Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune also have faint rings.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Armstrong. Not Buzz Aldrin, who followed him.

questions.text: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: 8.

questions.text: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: the Milky Way Galaxy.

questions.text: What do you call a person trained to travel into space?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: cosmonaut, taikonaut.

questions.text: Which former ninth planet was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
Which planet is closest to the Sun?
What is the curved path a planet follows around the Sun called?
What icy object grows a glowing tail as it nears the Sun?
questions.hostNotes: Not an asteroid or meteor.

questions.text: What do you call a group of stars that forms a recognizable pattern, like Orion?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: asterism.

questions.text: What is the scientific name for a "shooting star"?
questions.hostNotes: Not meteorite, which is a piece that reaches the ground.

questions.text: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.hostNotes: Not Mercury. Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.

questions.text: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.hostNotes: Not Pluto, which is now a dwarf planet.

questions.text: What was the name of the 1969 mission that first landed humans on the Moon?
questions.hostNotes: Must include "11".

questions.text: Who became the first human to travel into space, in 1961?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Gagarin. Not Neil Armstrong.

questions.text: What is a region of space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape?
What scientific theory says the universe began from an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Big Bang theory.

questions.text: What famous space telescope was launched into orbit in 1990?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Hubble. Not James Webb, launched in 2021.

questions.text: What do you call the powerful explosion of a dying star?
A light-year is a unit used to measure what?
questions.hostNotes: Not time. It is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.text: What type of eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth?
questions.hostNotes: Not a lunar eclipse, when Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

questions.text: What famous comet returns to Earth's skies roughly every 76 years?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Halley. It last appeared in 1986.

questions.text: What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Sputnik.

questions.text: Which planet rotates tipped on its side, so it seems to roll around the Sun?
What is the short name of the Philippine Space Agency, created in 2019?
questions.hostNotes: Not PSA, which is the Philippine Statistics Authority, or PAGASA.

questions.text: What was the name of the first Philippine-built microsatellite, launched in 2016?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Diwata. It was released into orbit from the International Space Station.

questions.text: Which Italian astronomer discovered Jupiter's four largest moons with a telescope in 1610?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Galileo. The four are called the Galilean moons.

questions.text: Which Polish astronomer proposed that the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Copernicus.

questions.text: Who became the first woman in space, in 1963?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tereshkova.

questions.text: What was the name of the Soviet dog who became the first animal to orbit Earth, in 1957?
To the nearest minute, about how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: eight minutes. It is about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

questions.text: The main asteroid belt lies between which two planets?
questions.hostNotes: Both needed, in either order.

questions.text: What is the nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Andromeda Galaxy, M31. Not the Magellanic Clouds, which are small satellite galaxies.

questions.text: What is the brightest star in the night sky?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Dog Star. Not Polaris, the North Star, which is not especially bright.

questions.text: Apart from the Sun, what is the closest star to Earth?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Alpha Centauri, the star system it belongs to.

questions.text: What is the largest volcano in the solar system, found on Mars?
What is the largest moon in the solar system?
questions.hostNotes: It orbits Jupiter. Not Titan, which is second.

questions.text: What are the names of the two moons of Mars?
questions.hostNotes: Both needed.

questions.text: What is the name of NASA's rover that landed on Mars in February 2021?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Percy. Not Curiosity, which landed in 2012.

questions.text: What is the outer atmosphere of the Sun, seen as a glowing halo during a total eclipse?
The Big Dipper is part of which constellation?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Great Bear. Not Ursa Minor, the Little Dipper.
